newsitem.title: UK: LVMH may seek brewing, food sale -paper.
newsitem.headline: LVMH may seek brewing, food sale -paper.

text.p: LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault may change tactics in his battle to scotch the planned 24 billion stg merger between Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc, The Independent newspaper reported on Wednesday.

It said Arnault, whose French luxury goods and drinks group is a substantial shareholder in both Guinness and GrandMet, might put forward plans to sell Guinness' brewing arm and GrandMet's Pillsbury and Burger King food businesses to trade buyers rather than spin them off as separate companies.
LVMH'S advisers, BZW, have already been contacted by several investment banks and rival companies expressing an interest in buying the businesses, the report said.
It said Arnault would also accept a deal whereby Burger King and Pillsbury were kept together as one company which would then be demerged.
Instead of a Guinness/Grand Met merger, Arnault wants to create a three-way wines and spirits mix of LVMH drinks division Moet Hennessey, Guinness drinks arm United Distillers and Grand Met's IDV.
GrandMet and Guinness have slammed the rival plan, saying Arnault's demerger proposals would result in tax costs of 1.5 billion stg.
